title: The Baltics in 13 Days: Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia from Riga to Tallinn
meta_title: Baltic Tour 13 Days: Riga, Vilnius, Tallinn, Curonian Spit
meta_description: 13-day Baltic road trip: Riga, Kuldīga, the Curonian Spit, Kaunas, Trakai Castle, Vilnius, Gauja valley, Seto villages, Tartu, Lahemaa, Tallinn and Pärnu.
tagline: Three countries, four UNESCO old towns, sand dunes, bogs and island castles
facts: Riga 1, Kuldīga 1, Klaipėda 1, Kaunas 1, Vilnius 2, Daugavpils 1, Sigulda 1, Võru 1, Tartu 1, Tallinn 1, Pärnu 1
Private car with driver, or self-drive
Active; mostly one night per stop
intro: A full loop of the three Baltic countries by road. From Riga west to Kemeri's bog and the waterfall town of Kuldīga, south to the dunes of the Curonian Spit, through Kaunas and Trakai's island castle to baroque Vilnius, then back north through Latgale's farmsteads, the Gauja valley, the Seto villages of south Estonia, university Tartu, Lahemaa National Park, Tallinn and the beach town of Pärnu. Most stops are one night, and Riga and Tallinn get less time than they deserve: we recommend adding a second night in Tallinn and a final night in Riga, making it 15 days.

Kemeri bog boardwalk and Kuldīga's wide waterfall

faqs.q: Can this itinerary be changed for our dates and pace?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Blue Diamond Voyage itinerary is a starting point. We change the number of nights, the hotels, the pace and the activities to suit your family, and send you a personalised quote.

faqs.q: Do you look after vegetarian and Jain food?
faqs.a: Yes. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and guide before you travel, and suggest pure-vegetarian restaurants along the route. Jain meals without onion, garlic and root vegetables can be arranged in most places with notice.

faqs.q: Is there support while we travel?
faqs.a: Yes. You have our 24/7 travel desk on +91 97148 59797 and +91 98242 21400 and a WhatsApp group with your consultant for the whole trip.

good_to_know.title: Hotel deposit
good_to_know.text: Use a credit card for the deposit or pre-authorisation at check-in, never a forex or debit card. Forex cards cannot hold funds, many hotels refuse them, and a credit-card hold is released faster.

good_to_know.title: Cards and cash
good_to_know.text: On card machines, always choose to pay in euros, never in INR. Cards work almost everywhere. Carry about EUR 50 in cash for small cafés, toilets and markets.

good_to_know.title: Pickpockets
good_to_know.text: Busy stations, trams and squares are pickpocket hotspots. Keep passports in the hotel safe, carry a copy, and wear your bag in front in crowds.

good_to_know.title: Plugs, water and meal times
good_to_know.text: Plugs are the two round-pin type C and F at 230 volts (Switzerland uses type J; a type C plug fits). Tap water is safe to drink. Lunch is about 12:00 to 14:00 and dinner from about 18:30.

dining_intro: Vegetarian food is easy to find in every city on this route; Jain meals take planning. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and tour, and list Indian and vegetarian restaurants near each hotel in your travel pack.
dining_avoid: Soups, sauces, risottos and even some vegetable dishes are often made with meat or fish stock, and many cheeses use animal rennet. Show the food card and ask before ordering.
food_card: We are strict vegetarians (Jain). No meat, fish, seafood or eggs. No onion, garlic, potato, carrot or any root vegetables. No meat or fish stock. Thank you.
